summary.en: Notifies attendees when meeting summaries are ready, restores source-channel cards for scheduled meetings, introduces fixed-version container images with runtime frontend configuration, and updates vulnerable dependencies.

description.en: Attendees receive a notification when a meeting summary first becomes ready. Opening the notification goes directly to the summary, and viewing a ready summary marks its notifications read. Editing or regenerating a summary does not send another completion notification; existing summaries do not trigger historical notifications during upgrade.

title.en: Scheduled meeting cards appear when the meeting starts

description.en: Starting a scheduled meeting creates its card in the source channel at the actual start time, including when a guest starts the meeting. Card creation retries after temporary failures without undoing a successful meeting start or creating duplicate cards. Existing channel access rules remain in force; historical meetings are not backfilled.

Official backend, frontend, and transcription-worker images support Linux AMD64 and ARM64 and share one fixed release version. Self-Hosting, Coolify, Dokploy, and Plesk deployments pull these images. Release assets record their immutable digests, and Plesk validates and downloads the selected images before switching the installation. Source-build overrides remain available for custom builds and branch testing.

title.en: Configure the frontend when its container starts

description.en: Set public API, socket, LiveKit, Web Push, and CSRF-cookie configuration without rebuilding the frontend image. Canonical environment variables take precedence over compatible VITE aliases, and invalid required configuration stops startup. The frontend runs without root privileges and supports a read-only filesystem; HTML and runtime configuration are served without caching.
Recording and transcription indicators use consistent theme colors for clearer text and status badges in light and dark mode.

Updates sharp to 0.35.5, Vue and its server renderer to 3.5.43, and source-map-js to 1.2.2. These updates address upstream image-decoding, server-rendering, and source-map advisories. The Vue advisory concerns server-side rendering; Nebulynk renders its application in the browser.

summary.en: Updates sharp and its bundled librsvg to address a use-after-free vulnerability when decoding crafted SVG images. Upstream describes possible code execution under specific Linux runtime conditions; this does not establish exploitability in every Nebulynk deployment.

Updates the Vue server-renderer dependency to address attribute-name validation that can permit cross-site scripting in server-rendered HTML. The vulnerable rendering path is not used by Nebulynk's browser-rendered application.

Updates the source-map-js build dependency to prevent excessive indexed source-map offsets from blocking the event loop. This concerns source-map processing rather than ordinary Nebulynk chat requests.

en: Before updating, create and verify external backups of PostgreSQL, both Garage volumes, and deployment configuration and secrets. Keep the existing persistent volumes. When upgrading from a version before 0.7.0, also review recording-retention and transcription-worker guidance: the default 60-day retention may delete eligible older recordings at startup.

Review the deployment files and container guide from the v0.7.2 tag before switching a source-built installation to images. Keep the existing Compose project or platform resource and volume mappings. Confirm the PostgreSQL database, storage, and resolved public API/socket URLs refer to the intended installation. Set NEBULYNK_VERSION=0.7.2 and deploy backend, frontend, and transcription-worker together. The standalone Compose files require Docker Compose 2.23.1 or newer; Plesk remains Linux x86-64 only.

Configure the frontend's public API_URL at container startup; compatible VITE aliases remain supported. Check existing API_URL, BACKEND_URL, and their VITE aliases for stale overrides before recreating the frontend. Recreate affected containers after changing environment values so the new runtime configuration is applied.

Stop the old backend completely before starting its replacement and allow at least 75 seconds for shutdown. Startup applies migrations 076_meeting_summary_notifications and 077_meeting_source_messages automatically. Wait for GET /health/ready and the worker health check to pass before reopening access.

After updating, verify login, recent chat history, uploads, a newly started scheduled meeting's source-channel card, and the first completion notification for a new meeting summary. Existing summaries and historical scheduled meetings are not backfilled. Check the frontend's rendered runtime configuration and API target when adopting the prebuilt images.
